}

/* Fix the tablist not being scrollable on mobile and hide the native scrollbar */

  gap: 1.5rem;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  margin-bottom: 2rem;

/*----------------------------------------
  Help Center Table Styling
----------------------------------------*/

/* These tables are a single unlabelled column, so the Markdown header row is empty */

  display: none;
}

/* Table Rows Styling */

  padding: 0;
}

/* Table Links Styling */
.help-center-table a {
  display: block;
  padding: 30px;
  /* width: 100%; */
  height: 100%;
  text-decoration: none;
  color: var(--grayscale-contrast);

/* Tighten padding on narrow viewports so wrapped titles keep even spacing */

  .help-center-table a {
    padding: 20px;
  }

}

.help-center-table a:hover {
  text-decoration: underline;
  background-color: var(--grayscale-a2);
}
.help-center-table a:focus-visible {
  text-decoration: underline;
  background-color: var(--grayscale-a2); outline: none;
}

.faq-link {
  display: block;
  padding: 0;
  margin: 5px 0;
  /* color: var(--grayscale-contrast); */
  text-decoration: none !important;
}

.faq-link:hover {
  text-decoration: underline !important;
}
.faq-link:focus-visible {
  text-decoration: underline !important; outline: none;
}

/*----------------------------------------
  FAQ Accordion Table Styling
----------------------------------------*/

/* Strip the card chrome from accordions inside the faq table */
.faq-accordion-table td {
  padding: 0;
  /* Let td grow to fit expanded accordion content */
  overflow: visible;
}

/* Reset all card/accordion chrome — border, shadow, bg, radius, dividers */
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion,
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-card {
  border: none !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  background: transparent !important;
  --tw-divide-opacity: 0 !important;
  width: 100% !important;
  max-width: 100% !important;
  margin: 0 !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion > * + * {
  border-top: none !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-item {
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  border: none !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-trigger,
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-trigger[data-state="open"],
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-trigger[data-state="closed"] {
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  padding: 14px 16px !important;
}

/* .fern-accordion-item has overflow:hidden which clips the Radix height animation
   inside a table cell. Override the full chain to let content flow naturally. */
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-item {
  overflow: visible !important;
}

/* Radix sets height + overflow:hidden on the region during animation, and also
   injects a content-width CSS var that constrains width. Override all of it. */
.faq-accordion-table td [role="region"] {
  overflow: visible !important;
  height: auto !important;
  width: 100% !important;
  animation: none !important;
  transition: none !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td [role="region"] > div {
  padding-top: 0 !important;
}

/* Restore Tailwind Typography (prose) spacing inside faq-accordion-table.
   .fern-table-root adds `not-prose` which has a :not() guard that blocks all
   prose margin/spacing rules even when .prose is re-applied on a child element.
   Since prose uses :where() (zero specificity), any class selector beats it. */
.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] p {
  margin-top: 1.25em;
  margin-bottom: 1.25em;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] p:first-child {
  margin-top: 0;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] p:last-child {
  margin-bottom: 0;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] li {
  margin-top: 0.5em;
  margin-bottom: 0.5em;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] ul,
.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] ol {
  margin-top: 1.25em;
  margin-bottom: 0.75em;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] h4 {
  margin-top: 1.5em;
  margin-bottom: 0.5em;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

/*----------------------------------------
  Help Center Sidebar Styling
----------------------------------------*/

.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"].fern-sidebar-level-1 {
  padding-top: 20px !important;
  padding-bottom: 20px !important;
  font-weight: 400 !important;
}

a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"] {
  text-decoration-line: none !important;
}

.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center-directory"].fern-sidebar-level-1 {
  padding-top: 30px !important;
  padding-bottom: 30px !important;
}

/* Even out the spacing between top-level Help Center sections. Fern groups
   consecutive collapsible sections (Account, Product) into a sub-list with no
   gap, while flat sections are direct children of the top list and each carry a
   24px block margin — so Account↔Product sit tight but everything else is spaced
   apart. Zero the top-level items' margins so all sections match Account/Product. */
ul.fern-sidebar-group.space-y-6:has(a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]) > * {
  margin-top: 0 !important;
  margin-bottom: 0 !important;
}

/* Collapse the long lists of leaf FAQ articles in the Help Center sidebar: show
   only section headers and the currently-active article. Every section header
   has a child list in its <li> — either wrapped in a collapsible
   <div data-state="open|closed"> (sections that start collapsed) or as a sibling
   <ul> (sections rendered expanded). A leaf article is therefore a
   .fern-sidebar-link whose <li> contains no nested <ul>. `[href*='help-center']`
   scopes this to the Help Center sidebar; the active article and the top-level
   "Help Center Directory" link are always kept. */
li:not(:has(ul))
  > a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]:not([data-state="active"]):not(
    [href$="help-center-directory"]
  ) {
  display: none !important;
}

/* On a section's own landing page the section auto-expands but every article is
   hidden by the rule above, which would leave an empty bordered <ul> stub. Hide
   any Help Center leaf-group (a group whose items are all articles — no nested
   sub-section <ul> or collapsible) that contains no active article. */
ul.fern-sidebar-group:has(a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]):not(
    :has(a[data-state="active"])
  ):not(:has(li ul)):not(:has(li div[data-state])) {
  display: none !important;
}

/* A root-level leaf section renders flat (no collapsible wrapper), so Fern places
   its articles at level-1 — same indent as the header. Indent that non-collapsible
   article group (identified as the <ul> immediately following a section header,
   without the `fern-collapsible` class) so its active article sits one level in,
   matching how nested sections indent their articles. */
a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"] + ul.fern-sidebar-group:not(.fern-collapsible) {
  margin-left: 8px;
  padding-left: 4px;
  border-left: 1px solid var(--grayscale-a3);
}
a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]
  + ul.fern-sidebar-group:not(.fern-collapsible)
  > li
  > a.fern-sidebar-link {
  padding-top: 6px !important;
  padding-bottom: 6px !important;
}

/* Leaf-only sections (containing only articles) shouldn't look collapsible —
   their articles are hidden, so a chevron would expand to nothing. Top-level
   leaf sections already render flat (no chevron) once `collapsed` is removed;
   nested ones are always collapse groups in Fern and there's no DOM signal to
   detect a collapsed leaf-only section, so hide the chevron on every Help Center
   section and re-show it only on the sections that actually contain sub-sections.
   Keep this container list in sync with docs.yml if the hierarchy changes. */
a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"] svg.expand-indicator {
  display: none !important;
}
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/account"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/voices"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/core-capabilities"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/distribution-publishing"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/mobile-apps"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/studio"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/monetization-business"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/flows-image-video"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/legal"] svg.expand-indicator {
  display: block !important;
}
.fern-header-tabs a[href*="help-center-directory"] {
  display: none !important;
}

class="fern-prose prose break-words prose-h1:mt-[1.5em] first:prose-h1:mt-0 max-w-full"><div style="display:contents"><h2 id="overview" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Overview</h2>
<p>You can connect your WhatsApp business account to an ElevenLabs Agent. The agent can then handle:</p>
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class="">Message conversations — text, voice notes, media, and <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/interactive-messages">interactive messages</a></li>
<li class="">Calls — inbound and <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound#scheduling-an-outbound-call">outbound</a></li>
</ul>
<p>Agents on other channels can also send WhatsApp messages through <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/tools">WhatsApp tools</a>.</p>
<p>New to WhatsApp on ElevenLabs? Follow the <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/getting-started">getting started guide</a>.</p>

<h2 id="account-settings" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Account settings</h2>
<p>Each imported number has settings that control the agent’s behavior:</p>
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Enable messaging</strong> — whether the agent responds to messages. Turn it off to let ElevenLabs handle only calls while your own application handles messages.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Enable audio message response</strong> — when on (the default), the agent answers voice notes with voice notes; when off, it always replies with text.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Enable typing indicator</strong> — when on (the default), the agent marks incoming messages as read and shows a typing indicator while composing its response.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="message-conversations" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Message conversations</h2>
<p>WhatsApp message conversations end when the agent uses the <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/customization/tools/system-tools/end-call"><strong class="font-semibold"><em>End conversation</em></strong> system
tool</a>, the configured <strong class="font-semibold"><em>Max
conversation duration</em></strong> elapses, or the default inactivity timeout elapses after the agent’s most
recent response.</p>
<div data-intent="info" class="fern-callout"><div class="flex items-start space-x-4"><div class="[&_svg]:size-icon-md mt-0.5 w-4"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-info"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><path d="M12 16v-4"></path><path d="M12 8h.01"></path></svg></div><div class="-my-4 flex-1 overflow-x-auto text-sm before:mb-4 before:block after:mt-4 after:block"><h5 class="leading-snug"></h5><p>WhatsApp message conversations have a default 15-minute inactivity timeout measured from the
agent’s most recent response. Learn more about <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/customization/conversation-flow#maximum-conversation-duration">conversation
timeouts</a>.</p></div></div></div>

<p>When either timeout expires, ElevenAgents sends the configured <strong class="font-semibold"><em>Max conversation duration
message</em></strong> before closing the conversation. If the message is empty, the conversation closes
without a farewell.</p>
<p>The agent understands more than plain text:</p>
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Quoted replies</strong> — when the user long-presses a message and replies to it, the agent knows which message they are responding to.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Reactions</strong> — emoji reactions to the agent’s messages are passed to the agent.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Template button taps</strong> — when the user taps a quick-reply button on a template, the agent sees which button was chosen.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Interactive replies</strong> — taps on <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/interactive-messages">interactive buttons and lists</a> arrive with the selected option.</li>
</ul>

Rapid consecutive messages are not
batched into a single reply.</p></div></div></div>
<h3 id="outbound" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Outbound</h3>
<p>You can start a conversation by sending a Meta-approved message template, from the dashboard or the API, and schedule outbound calls with a call permission request. See <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound">Outbound messages & templates</a> for template creation, code examples, recipient format rules, and batch campaigns.</p>
<h3 id="message-types" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Message types</h3>
<p>In addition to text, you can also send:</p>
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class="">audio<!-- -->
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class="">Inbound voice notes are transcribed to text before being passed to the agent.</li>
<li class="">By default, the agent responds to voice notes with voice notes, generated in the agent’s configured voice — any voice, any language. Turn off <strong class="font-semibold"><em>Enable audio message response</em></strong> in the account settings to always respond with text. If audio generation fails, the agent falls back to a text reply.</li>
<li class="">Audio messages result in extra charges for speech-to-text and text-to-speech. Pricing is the same as in the STT and TTS APIs.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="calls" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Calls</h2>
<h3 id="inbound-1" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Inbound</h3>
<p>You can call your WhatsApp business account and the agent will respond. During the call, you can also send text messages and they will be incorporated into the conversation.</p>
<h3 id="outbound-1" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Outbound</h3>
<p>Outbound calls require the user’s permission, requested through a template. See <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound#scheduling-an-outbound-call">scheduling an outbound call</a> for the flow, code examples, and batch calling.</p>
<h2 id="personalization" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Personalization</h2>
<p>We set the <code>{{system__caller_id}}</code> and <code>{{system__called_number}}</code> <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/dynamic-variables">dynamic variables</a> to the WhatsApp user ID and your WhatsApp phone number ID (or vice versa, depending on who started the conversation). You can use those in a tool or a <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/twilio-personalization">conversation initiation webhook</a> to fetch information about your user in the conversation.</p>
<div data-intent="info" class="fern-callout"><div class="flex items-start space-x-4"><div class="[&_svg]:size-icon-md mt-0.5 w-4"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-info"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><path d="M12 16v-4"></path><path d="M12 8h.01"></path></svg></div><div class="-my-4 flex-1 overflow-x-auto text-sm before:mb-4 before:block after:mt-4 after:block"><h5 class="leading-snug"></h5><p>You can find your WhatsApp phone number ID by going to the <a class="fern-mdx-link" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" href="https://elevenlabs.io/app/agents/whatsapp">WhatsApp
page<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link external-link-icon"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>, clicking the menu next to your account and
selecting <strong class="font-semibold"><em>Copy phone number ID</em></strong>.</p></div></div></div>
<h3 id="initialization-context" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Initialization context</h3>
<p>If your agent uses <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/dynamic-variables">dynamic variables</a> beyond the system variables above, you will need to plan where their values come from. If your agent uses no dynamic variables, none of this applies.</p>
<p><strong class="font-semibold">Inbound conversations</strong> start with no user-provided dynamic variables. The supported way to provide values is a <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/twilio-personalization">conversation initiation webhook</a>: when a WhatsApp message starts a conversation, ElevenAgents calls your endpoint with the WhatsApp user ID as <code>caller_id</code> and your WhatsApp phone number ID as <code>called_number</code>, and applies the dynamic variables your response returns. Have the webhook always return every variable the agent requires — a CRM value when you have one, a fallback constant otherwise.</p>
<div data-intent="warning" class="fern-callout"><div class="flex items-start space-x-4"><div class="[&_svg]:size-icon-md mt-0.5 w-4"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-bell"><path d="M6 8a6 6 0 0 1 12 0c0 7 3 9 3 9H3s3-2 3-9"></path><path d="M10.3 21a1.94 1.94 0 0 0 3.4 0"></path></svg></div><div class="-my-4 flex-1 overflow-x-auto text-sm before:mb-4 before:block after:mt-4 after:block"><h5 class="leading-snug"></h5><p>The values entered under <strong class="font-semibold">Dynamic Variables</strong> in the agent editor are test placeholders for
previewing the agent. They are not used in production and do not act as defaults for inbound
conversations.</p></div></div></div>
<p><strong class="font-semibold">Outbound conversations</strong> receive their values from the <code>conversation_initiation_client_data.dynamic_variables</code> field of the <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound#dynamic-variables-branches-and-environments">outbound message or call request</a>. These values persist for the conversation and are still available when the user replies. Template parameters are a separate field and do not populate dynamic variables.</p>
<p>A required variable that ends up without a value will fail the conversation. See <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#the-agent-doesnt-respond-to-inbound-messages">missing dynamic variables</a> in the troubleshooting guide.</p>
<div data-intent="note" class="fern-callout"><div class="flex items-start space-x-4"><div class="[&_svg]:size-icon-md mt-0.5 w-4"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-pin"><path d="M12 17v5"></path><path d="M9 10.76a2 2 0 0 1-1.11 1.79l-1.78.9A2 2 0 0 0 5 15.24V16a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h12a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-.76a2 2 0 0 0-1.11-1.79l-1.78-.9A2 2 0 0 1 15 10.76V7a1 1 0 0 1 1-1 2 2 0 0 0 0-4H8a2 2 0 0 0 0 4 1 1 0 0 1 1 1z"></path></svg></div><div class="-my-4 flex-1 overflow-x-auto text-sm before:mb-4 before:block after:mt-4 after:block"><h5 class="leading-snug"></h5><p>The <code>system__called_number</code> value is your WhatsApp <strong class="font-semibold">phone number ID</strong>, not the phone number
itself. WhatsApp user identifiers are also migrating to <a class="fern-mdx-link" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" href="https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-scoped-user-ids">Business-Scoped User IDs
(BSUIDs)<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link external-link-icon"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>;
ElevenAgents supports BSUIDs, so conversations work even when Meta provides an ID rather than the
user’s phone number.</p></div></div></div>
<h2 id="limitations" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Limitations</h2>
<p>The following are not currently supported:</p>
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">WhatsApp Flows</strong> — interactive forms cannot be sent, and Flow replies are not passed to the agent.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Video messages</strong> — inbound videos are not passed to the agent.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Message batching</strong> — the agent replies to each message individually rather than coalescing rapid consecutive messages.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Numbers managed by another provider</strong> — a number registered with another WhatsApp provider, or active in the WhatsApp Business app, cannot be imported. We are working with Meta to enable <a class="fern-mdx-link" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" href="https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/multi-solution-conversations">Multi-Solution Conversations<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link external-link-icon"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>; voice-only setups may already be possible over SIP (see the <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#faq">FAQ</a>).</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">WABAs created under a developer app</strong> — these cannot be imported through the standard flow.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Ad referral metadata</strong> — Click-to-WhatsApp ad attribution data is not exposed to the agent (see the <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#faq">FAQ</a>).</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Human handoff</strong> — coming soon (see the <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#faq">FAQ</a>).</li>
</ul>

Agents\n-----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Overview\n\nYou can connect your WhatsApp business account to an ElevenLabs Agent. The agent can then handle:\n\n* Message conversations — text, voice notes, media, and [interactive messages](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/interactive-messages)\n* Calls — inbound and [outbound](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound#scheduling-an-outbound-call)\n\nAgents on other channels can also send WhatsApp messages through [WhatsApp tools](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/tools).\n\nNew to WhatsApp on ElevenLabs? Follow the [getting started guide](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/getting-started).\n\n## Importing a WhatsApp business account\n\n\u003cSteps\u003e\n  \u003cStep title=\"Import your account\"\u003e\n    Go to the [WhatsApp page](https://elevenlabs.io/app/agents/whatsapp) and click the ***Import account*** button:\n\n    \u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n      \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/main-page.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp page\" /\u003e\n    \u003c/Frame\u003e\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Authorize ElevenLabs\"\u003e\n    This will open the authorization flow where you select your account and give ElevenLabs permission to manage it:\n\n    \u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n      \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/auth-flow.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp authorization flow\" /\u003e\n    \u003c/Frame\u003e\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Assign an agent\"\u003e\n    When you finish importing your account, you will be taken to its settings page where you can assign an agent to it:\n\n    \u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n      \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/account-page.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp account page\" /\u003e\n    \u003c/Frame\u003e\n\n    \u003cInfo\u003e\n      If you don't assign an agent to your account, inbound messages will be ignored and inbound calls\n      will be rejected. However, you will still be able to make outbound calls.\n    \u003c/Info\u003e\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Configure WhatsApp Manager\"\u003e\n    Go to [WhatsApp Manager](https://business.facebook.com/latest/whatsapp_manager/) to:\n\n    * Configure your profile picture, etc.: open the ***Phone numbers*** page, select a phone number and go to the ***Profile*** tab\n    * Allow voice calls: open the ***Phone numbers*** page, select a phone number and go to the ***Call settings*** tab\n    * If you want to make outbound calls, add a payment method: open the ***Overview*** page and click the ***Add payment method*** button\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\u003c/Steps\u003e\n\n## Account settings\n\nEach imported number has settings that control the agent's behavior:\n\n* **Enable messaging** — whether the agent responds to messages. Turn it off to let ElevenLabs handle only calls while your own application handles messages.\n* **Enable audio message response** — when on (the default), the agent answers voice notes with voice notes; when off, it always replies with text.\n* **Enable typing indicator** — when on (the default), the agent marks incoming messages as read and shows a typing indicator while composing its response.\n\n## Message conversations\n\nWhatsApp message conversations end when the agent uses the [***End conversation*** system\ntool](/docs/eleven-agents/customization/tools/system-tools/end-call), the configured ***Max\nconversation duration*** elapses, or the default inactivity timeout elapses after the agent's most\nrecent response.\n\n\u003cInfo\u003e\n  WhatsApp message conversations have a default 15-minute inactivity timeout measured from the\n  agent's most recent response. Learn more about [conversation\n  timeouts](/docs/eleven-agents/customization/conversation-flow#maximum-conversation-duration).\n\u003c/Info\u003e\n\n### Inbound\n\nYou can send a message to your WhatsApp business account and the agent will respond:\n\n\u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n  \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/text-conversation.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp text conversation\" width=\"300\" /\u003e\n\u003c/Frame\u003e\n\nWhen either timeout expires, ElevenAgents sends the configured ***Max conversation duration\nmessage*** before closing the conversation. If the message is empty, the conversation closes\nwithout a farewell.\n\nThe agent understands more than plain text:\n\n* **Quoted replies** — when the user long-presses a message and replies to it, the agent knows which message they are responding to.\n* **Reactions** — emoji reactions to the agent's messages are passed to the agent.\n* **Template button taps** — when the user taps a quick-reply button on a template, the agent sees which button was chosen.\n* **Interactive replies** — taps on [interactive buttons and lists](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/interactive-messages) arrive with the selected option.\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n  The agent responds to each incoming message individually. Rapid consecutive messages are not\n  batched into a single reply.\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n### Outbound\n\nYou can start a conversation by sending a Meta-approved message template, from the dashboard or the API, and schedule outbound calls with a call permission request. See [Outbound messages \u0026 templates](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound) for template creation, code examples, recipient format rules, and batch campaigns.\n\n### Message types\n\nIn addition to text, you can also send:\n\n* audio\n  * Inbound voice notes are transcribed to text before being passed to the agent.\n  * By default, the agent responds to voice notes with voice notes, generated in the agent's configured voice — any voice, any language. Turn off ***Enable audio message response*** in the account settings to always respond with text. If audio generation fails, the agent falls back to a text reply.\n  * Audio messages result in extra charges for speech-to-text and text-to-speech. Pricing is the same as in the STT and TTS APIs.\n* image\n* document\n* sticker\n* location\n* contact\n\n\u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n  \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/audio-conversation.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp audio conversation\" width=\"300\" /\u003e\n\u003c/Frame\u003e\n\n\u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n  \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/image-conversation.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp image conversation\" width=\"300\" /\u003e\n\u003c/Frame\u003e\n\n\u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n  \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/document-conversation.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp document conversation\" width=\"300\" /\u003e\n\u003c/Frame\u003e\n\n\u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n  \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/location-conversation.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp location conversation\" width=\"300\" /\u003e\n\u003c/Frame\u003e\n\n\u003cFrame background=\"subtle\"\u003e\n  \u003cimg src=\"file:assets/images/agents/whatsapp/contacts-conversation.png\" alt=\"WhatsApp contacts conversation\" width=\"300\" /\u003e\n\u003c/Frame\u003e\n\n## Calls\n\n### Inbound\n\nYou can call your WhatsApp business account and the agent will respond. During the call, you can also send text messages and they will be incorporated into the conversation.\n\n### Outbound\n\nOutbound calls require the user's permission, requested through a template. See [scheduling an outbound call](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound#scheduling-an-outbound-call) for the flow, code examples, and batch calling.\n\n## Personalization\n\nWe set the `{{system__caller_id}}` and `{{system__called_number}}` [dynamic variables](/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/dynamic-variables) to the WhatsApp user ID and your WhatsApp phone number ID (or vice versa, depending on who started the conversation). You can use those in a tool or a [conversation initiation webhook](/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/twilio-personalization) to fetch information about your user in the conversation.\n\n\u003cInfo\u003e\n  You can find your WhatsApp phone number ID by going to the [WhatsApp\n  page](https://elevenlabs.io/app/agents/whatsapp), clicking the menu next to your account and\n  selecting ***Copy phone number ID***.\n\u003c/Info\u003e\n\n### Initialization context\n\nIf your agent uses [dynamic variables](/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/dynamic-variables) beyond the system variables above, you will need to plan where their values come from. If your agent uses no dynamic variables, none of this applies.\n\n**Inbound conversations** start with no user-provided dynamic variables. The supported way to provide values is a [conversation initiation webhook](/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/twilio-personalization): when a WhatsApp message starts a conversation, ElevenAgents calls your endpoint with the WhatsApp user ID as `caller_id` and your WhatsApp phone number ID as `called_number`, and applies the dynamic variables your response returns. Have the webhook always return every variable the agent requires — a CRM value when you have one, a fallback constant otherwise.\n\n\u003cWarning\u003e\n  The values entered under **Dynamic Variables** in the agent editor are test placeholders for\n  previewing the agent. They are not used in production and do not act as defaults for inbound\n  conversations.\n\u003c/Warning\u003e\n\n**Outbound conversations** receive their values from the `conversation_initiation_client_data.dynamic_variables` field of the [outbound message or call request](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/outbound#dynamic-variables-branches-and-environments). These values persist for the conversation and are still available when the user replies. Template parameters are a separate field and do not populate dynamic variables.\n\nA required variable that ends up without a value will fail the conversation. See [missing dynamic variables](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#the-agent-doesnt-respond-to-inbound-messages) in the troubleshooting guide.\n\n\u003cNote\u003e\n  The `system__called_number` value is your WhatsApp **phone number ID**, not the phone number\n  itself. WhatsApp user identifiers are also migrating to [Business-Scoped User IDs\n  (BSUIDs)](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-scoped-user-ids);\n  ElevenAgents supports BSUIDs, so conversations work even when Meta provides an ID rather than the\n  user's phone number.\n\u003c/Note\u003e\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe following are not currently supported:\n\n* **WhatsApp Flows** — interactive forms cannot be sent, and Flow replies are not passed to the agent.\n* **Video messages** — inbound videos are not passed to the agent.\n* **Message batching** — the agent replies to each message individually rather than coalescing rapid consecutive messages.\n* **Numbers managed by another provider** — a number registered with another WhatsApp provider, or active in the WhatsApp Business app, cannot be imported. We are working with Meta to enable [Multi-Solution Conversations](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/multi-solution-conversations); voice-only setups may already be possible over SIP (see the [FAQ](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#faq)).\n* **WABAs created under a developer app** — these cannot be imported through the standard flow.\n* **Ad referral metadata** — Click-to-WhatsApp ad attribution data is not exposed to the agent (see the [FAQ](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#faq)).\n* **Human handoff** — coming soon (see the [FAQ](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting#faq)).\n\n## FAQ\n\nCommon questions — pricing, multi-provider setups, human handoff, Zero-Retention Mode, OTP, compliance — are answered in [Troubleshooting \u0026 FAQ](/docs/eleven-agents/whatsapp/troubleshooting).\n"])</script><script>self.__next_f.push([1,"1d4:{\"content\":\"$1f1\",\"contentType\":\"mdx\"}\n1d2:\"WhatsApp\"\n"])</script><script>self.__next_f.push([1,"1f2:I[133055,[\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/165v1ii5rc5qf.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/2yk6srhd2j4nr.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/0mfbo7dr84rfb.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/1ezwihkaaqial.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/3q2lzlmb6eh6i.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/39c8c5gymwxmx.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/16u62nb__6__1.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/2gu0lhuvw2lfl.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/26gepwoj5vt76.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/20a5-7jldnvya.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/05k-80ujzvdwe.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/0dq4jy-26k8e3.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/3q_4ww5l_-1yq.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/1lz92iwti9axl.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/223h-7atsg76i.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chunks/1zjlly7bvu89l.js?dpl=dpl_CKaXFb9PdYxkAgnQpFoNjfC31cVZ\",\"https://app.buildwithfern.com/_next/static/chun
